subject.title: [Feature]:  Missing Session Management Commands in OpenClaw

question: Which first-class session lifecycle contract should OpenClaw expose for this request: narrow wrappers around existing abort/delete/cleanup/compact, a hard-kill and resource-control model, or a staged split across narrower issues?
rationale: The requested behavior affects session state, process ownership, operator authority, security boundaries, and UI semantics, so code inspection cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Stage a narrow lifecycle contract
options.body: Start with maintainer-approved stop/kill semantics and split pause/resume/resource quotas into follow-up issues once the security model is clear.

options.title: Ship wrappers for existing primitives
options.body: Expose CLI/UI around current abort/delete/cleanup/compact behavior while documenting that these are not a full hard-kill or resource-governance boundary.

options.title: Design the full lifecycle system
options.body: Treat this as a larger session-control project covering hard kill, pause/resume, resource limits, UI, and audit/security semantics before implementation.

recommendation.title: Stage a narrow lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Start with maintainer-approved stop/kill semantics and split pause/resume/resource quotas into follow-up issues once the security model is clear.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged session management/dashboard API work is the strongest provenance signal for the affected contract surface.
